"'''Get Busy'''" is a song by Jamaican [[dancehall]] singer [[Sean Paul]], from his album ''[[Dutty Rock]]''. The song was one of the many hits from the jumpy [[Clapping|handclap]] [[riddim]] known as the [[Diwali Riddim]], produced by then-newcomer [[Steven Marsden]], and was the only song that never made the "Diwali" rhythm album on [[Greensleeves Records]].

Paul described it as "mainly a party song. It's not all about smoking weed". Originally released as a [[7-inch single]] in 1999,<ref>{{cite AV media notes|title=Get Busy|year=1999|type=US 7-inch single vinyl disc|publisher=[[VP Records]]|id=VPS 8780}}</ref> "Get Busy" was released internationally in 2003 and topped the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for three weeks that May. It also reached number one in Italy and the Netherlands, becoming a top-10 hit in an additional 11 countries. On 10 May 2003, the song was performed on ''[[Saturday Night Live]]''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Tropiano |first1=Stephen |title=Saturday Night Live FAQ |date=November 2013 |publisher=Applause |isbn=9781480366862 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wtGGDwAAQBAJ}}</ref>

"Get Busy" is a song by Jamaican dancehall singer Sean Paul, from his album Dutty Rock. The song was one of the many hits from the jumpy handclap riddim known as the Diwali Riddim, produced by then-newcomer Steven Marsden, and was the only song that never made the "Diwali" rhythm album on Greensleeves Records.

Paul described it as "mainly a party song. It's not all about smoking weed". Originally released as a 7-inch single in 1999, "Get Busy" was released internationally in 2003 and topped the US Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks that May. It also reached number one in Italy and the Netherlands, becoming a top-10 hit in an additional 11 countries. On 10 May 2003, the song was performed on Saturday Night Live.

sections.heading: Remix
sections.wikitext:
The official remix, "Get Busy (Clap Your Hands Now Remix)", features [[Fatman Scoop]] and the Crooklyn Clan, the remix uses the instrumental of Paul's previous single, "[[Gimme the Light]]", on the near end of the song.

In 2024, an official remix was released by [[Odd Mob]], titled "Get Busy (Odd Mob Club Mix)".<ref>{{cite news |title=Meet the Australian DJ Who's Officially Reworked a Sean Paul Hit |url=https://au.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/odd-mob-sean-paul-get-busy-mix-60355/ |access-date=8 July 2025 |work=Rolling Stone Australia |date=23 May 2024 |language=en-AU}}</ref> The remix was certified Gold by [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] (ARIA) in 2025.<ref name="ARIA25s"/>
sections.text:
The official remix, "Get Busy (Clap Your Hands Now Remix)", features Fatman Scoop and the Crooklyn Clan, the remix uses the instrumental of Paul's previous single, "Gimme the Light", on the near end of the song.

In 2024, an official remix was released by Odd Mob, titled "Get Busy (Odd Mob Club Mix)". The remix was certified Gold by Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) in 2025.

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
The video for "Get Busy" (directed by [[Little X]]) was shot in [[Woodbridge, Ontario]], and released in February 2003. The video was also nominated for two [[MTV Video Music Awards]] for Best Dance Video and Best New Artist in 2003. The video shows people dancing to the song at a basement house party, with some partygoers banging on duct pipes until the homeowner comes down to warn them to stop the banging. At the end of the video Paul's brother Jason introduces a song, noting it as a brand new single, and Paul then sings part of "[[Like Glue]]". Shortly into the second song, renewed banging on the pipes leads the homeowner to come back down to the basement and declare the party over. [[Kardinal Offishall]] makes a cameo appearance in the video.

On 9 December 2002, 21-year-old Ramesh Christie, a man watching the video shoot, was shot and killed by unidentified assailants.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Billboard |date=2002-12-10 |title=Man Murdered At Sean Paul Video Shoot |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/music-news/man-murdered-at-sean-paul-video-shoot-73185/ |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=Billboard |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=NME |date=2002-12-11 |title=ONLOOKER KILLED WATCHING SEAN PAUL VIDEO SHOOT |url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/nme-1931-1383918 |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=NME |language=en-GB}}</ref>

sections.heading: In popular culture
sections.wikitext:
{{In popular culture|date=September 2018}}
The song was used in the ''DANCE! Online'' online game, and in the game ''[[Dance Dance Revolution Extreme 2]]''.  The song's remix was played in the club scene of the 2003 film ''[[Grind (2003 film)|Grind]]''. The song also briefly appeared in the season two episode of ''[[The Wire]]'', ''[[Hot Shots (The Wire)|Hot Shots]]''. The song was used in ''[[DJ Hero 2]]''. The song was featured in a scene from the 2004 film ''[[Chasing Liberty]]''. An instrumental version of the song appeared on the [[Booze Cruise (The Office)|11th episode]] of the [[The Office (American season 2)|season 2]] of ''[[The Office (American TV series)|The Office]]''. The song was also played in a dance scene in the film ''[[Baby Mama (film)|Baby Mama]]''. The song also featured in a scene in the season two episode of ''[[Bad Education (TV series)|Bad Education]]''.
sections.text:
{{In popular culture|date=September 2018}}
The song was used in the DANCE! Online online game, and in the game Dance Dance Revolution Extreme 2.  The song's remix was played in the club scene of the 2003 film Grind. The song also briefly appeared in the season two episode of The Wire, Hot Shots. The song was used in DJ Hero 2. The song was featured in a scene from the 2004 film Chasing Liberty. An instrumental version of the song appeared on the 11th episode of the season 2 of The Office. The song was also played in a dance scene in the film Baby Mama. The song also featured in a scene in the season two episode of Bad Education.
